title: Van der Linde wins Zolder Race 1 as Abt takes a one-two
dek: Kelvin van der Linde led from pole to win DTM Race 1 at Zolder by 0.696 seconds for Abt Sportsline, with Rockenfeller second and Albon, on a long first stint, third.

chapters.title: Back to the old Belgian circuit with a points lead to defend
text: The DTM arrived at Zolder on 7–8 August with Kelvin van der Linde leading the championship for Abt Sportsline. The South African had been robbed of a victory at the Lausitzring by a technical problem, a round where Philip Ellis won Race 1 for Winward Mercedes-AMG and Maximilian Götz also took a win for HRT. His closest points rival was the Red Bull AF Corse Ferrari of 19-year-old Liam Lawson, whose own chance of a second win at the Lausitzring had slipped away when a pit-exit problem cost him the lead.

Zolder brought changes to the grid. Christian Klien made his DTM debut for JP Motorsport, and with it McLaren’s: the 720S GT3 was the first McLaren in the series, run by the former Formula 1 driver as part of a part-season programme ahead of a possible full entry in 2022. The car was given a balance-of-performance boost after Friday practice. Esteban Muth, the 19-year-old Belgian, was racing at home for T3 Motorsport and ran an art livery designed by Princess Delphine of Belgium. Alex Albon, the Red Bull Formula 1 reserve, picked up a five-place grid penalty for speeding under a red flag in Friday practice.

Abt had the advantage of preparation: van der Linde said the team had tested at Zolder a couple of weeks earlier and arrived well prepared, though he was curious how the order would look once everybody had track time on Sunday. The weekend was the third of the season and the fifth race, on a circuit where overtaking is known to be hard, so a place on the front rows and the timing of the mandatory stop mattered more than usual.

chapters.title: Pole by 0.021 seconds on a drying track
text: Qualifying was delayed by seven minutes so the track could dry completely, and the pit lane opened at 10:07 with a few wet patches still visible. Timo Glock’s Rowe BMW was the first below 1m30s, then Nico Müller’s Rosberg Audi set the early best at 1m27.735s. Mike Rockenfeller improved to 1m27.548s, and Sheldon van der Linde took the top spot in the second Rowe BMW with a 1m27.499s before the final five-minute dash, when the track was driest.

Götz then set a lap nearly half a second clear of the rest, but Kelvin van der Linde beat it by 0.021 seconds with a 1m27.054s, his second pole of the season. Götz’s HRT Mercedes #4 started second on 1m27.075s. Marco Wittmann’s Walkenhorst BMW was third, 0.136 seconds off, his best qualifying of the year.

Albon had qualified fourth, a career best at 1m27.225s and 0.171 seconds from pole, but his five-place penalty dropped him to ninth on the grid and promoted Abril, whose Mercedes #5 qualified fifth, to fourth. Rockenfeller, 1m27.256s, Ellis, 1m27.272s, Muth and Müller, both 1m27.340s, followed. Klien qualified 16th, over a second off the pace on the McLaren’s debut, and Glock’s Rowe BMW #16 was last of the 20 cars on 1m28.529s.

chapters.title: A first-corner melee ends Lawson’s race
text: Van der Linde held the lead into the first corner while Wittmann, fast away, passed Götz for second. Lawson, the championship’s second-placed driver, had made a slow start and was dropping into the midfield when he tried to avoid the melee at the chicane and was hit from behind by Arjun Maini’s GetSpeed Mercedes #36. Daniel Juncadella’s Gruppe M Mercedes #8 collided with Maini’s car in the same incident. All three cars were out, Lawson’s Ferrari #30 after one lap, and the safety car was deployed.

The neutralisation was prolonged. Racing resumed with a rolling start on lap 6, and Wittmann nearly drew alongside the leader through the first corner, but van der Linde had the inside line into Turn 2 and kept the lead. Lawson, who said there was nothing he could do, was left to look ahead to Sunday, with van der Linde’s lead over him standing at 32 points after the race.

chapters.title: Albon stays out, Wittmann is overcut
text: A large proportion of the field came in for fresh tyres straight after the restart. Abril stopped a lap earlier than van der Linde and Wittmann, who dived into the pit lane together on lap 7 and rejoined nose to tail, but Abril’s HRT Mercedes passed Wittmann on cold tyres at Bianchibocht.

The pivotal calls came from those who stayed out. Rockenfeller and Albon ran longer on their first stint, and Albon, who with the AF Corse team had planned to find clean air if everyone else pitted, lapped as quickly as the leaders on older tyres. After their stops, Rockenfeller’s Abt Audi #9 and Albon’s Ferrari came out ahead of both Abril and Wittmann, which left a three-way fight for the win between van der Linde, Rockenfeller and Albon. Albon’s own stop was imperfect, as he stalled leaving the pits and lost one to two seconds.

chapters.title: Albon has the pace but no way past
text: Albon had the freshest tyres of the three and shadowed the Abt pair for the rest of the race, but could not get a move to stick. Rockenfeller, the 2013 champion, defended with routine and class, and the race was extended to make up the time lost under the safety car, which ran it to 39 laps. Van der Linde won by 0.696 seconds from Rockenfeller, with Albon about a second further back in the closest finish of the 2021 season to that point. It was Abt’s first one-two of the season, van der Linde’s second win in five DTM starts and Albon’s first podium on the road, since his third place at Monza only came after Abril’s disqualification.

“In any other track we could have won this race,” Albon said. Abril held fourth from Wittmann, who took fifth, and Muth passed Ellis and then Götz to take sixth in his home race, ahead of the HRT Mercedes #4 that had started from the front row. Ellis was eighth, Lucas Auer ninth and Müller tenth, which meant five different brands in the first six. Klien was 12th on his debut, 1.5 seconds clear of Esmee Hawkey’s T3 Lamborghini. Van der Linde left with 97 points, 32 clear of Lawson on 65, with Götz third on 54.

facts.t: Closest finish of the season so far
facts.v: Van der Linde, Rockenfeller and Albon crossed the line almost nose to tail, with 0.696 seconds between the winner and second place.
Van der Linde beat Götz by 0.021 seconds in qualifying, his second pole of 2021, and Wittmann was third at 0.136 seconds.
Christian Klien qualified 16th in the first DTM race for McLaren and finished 12th in the JP Motorsport 720S GT3 despite a BoP boost after Friday practice.

facts.t: Five brands in the top six
facts.v: Audi, Ferrari, Mercedes-AMG, BMW and Lamborghini finished in the first six places, with Esteban Muth the highest Lamborghini in his home race.
Van der Linde finished the race on 97 points, ahead of Lawson on 65 and Götz on 54.
